issue.title: `useRoute().params.param` evaluates to `undefined` on navigation from `/:param` to `/` when using nested `<router-view />`
issue.body:
### Version
4.1.6

### Reproduction link
[stackblitz.com](https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-qd21wy?file=src%2Fmain.ts,src%2FHome.vue,src%2FParam.vue&terminal=dev)

--> Open in New Tab and open Console in DevTools.


### Steps to reproduce
1. Use router with subroutes under a nested RouterView (from 'vue-router')
```ts
{
  path: '/routerView/',
  component: RouterView,
  children: [
    {
      path: '',
      component: Home,
    },
    {
      path: ':param',
      component: Param,
    },
  ],
},
```
2. Watch `useRoute().params.param` inside `Param.vue`

### What is expected?
Watching `useRoute().params.param` does not trigger when going from `/routerView/123` to `/routerView`.

### What is actually happening?
`useRoute().params.param` evaluates to `undefined` when navigating from `/routerView/123` to `/routerView`.

### Additional comments

When a nested `<router-view />` (`component: RouterView`) isn't used, it works as expected.

same code with Vue v2.x do not show `"fetch foo: ", undefined`.
https://jsfiddle.net/s74dutkm/1/

### What is expected?
watcher for a route param is not called when a user leaved the route (same as v2)

### What is actually happening?
watcher for a route param is called when a user leaved the route (watcher gets `undefined` as the route param)

---
it may be caused by [this breaking change](https://github.com/vuejs/vue-next/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#breaking-changes).

I don't think it's natural that we need to consider the possibility a route param is `undefined` in a route which requires the param.

issue.title: Add `flush: pre` instead of `flush: post` breaking change to Vue 3 Migration Guide
issue.body:
Hey, I just migrated a bigger project to Vue 3 and was wondering why the above mentioned breaking change wasn't part of the migration guide since for me it was one of the biggest changes (or did I oversee it? 🤔). It has a big impact in when watchers are called, especially when the watcher fires requests.

Would be great to have this added to the guide so others can benefit from it!

Here are the necessary links:
- [Changelog](https://github.com/vuejs/core/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#breaking-changes-3)
- [Commit](https://github.com/vuejs/core/commit/49bb44756fda0a7019c69f2fa6b880d9e41125aa)
- [Issue](https://github.com/vuejs/core/issues/1706#issuecomment-666258948)

issue.title: Route update unexpectedly triggers watchers
issue.body:
### Reproduction

https://jsfiddle.net/sj1chxmd/2/

### Steps to reproduce the bug

Observe behaviour in this repro (Vue 2.7): https://jsfiddle.net/sj1chxmd/2/
Then compare the behaviour in this repro (Vue 3): https://jsfiddle.net/sf2gutkr/1/

### Expected behavior

The behaviour should be the same between the two examples.

### Actual behavior

The presence of a reactive variable on the `<router-view>` in the Vue 3 version forces its descendants' watchers to update. I believe the correct behaviour should be the Vue 2.7 behaviour.

### Additional information

Related:

- https://github.com/vuejs/vue-router/issues/3393
- https://github.com/vuejs/router/issues/1590

body: @posva since you closed my issue can you offer a signal of intent for this issue? This is marked as a minor issue but anybody migrating from Vue 2 is probably experiencing this issue whether they realize it or not. Our code base consists of thousands of components across hundreds of pages. It’s not possible to test the fallout from this bug, the surface area is pretty much everything.
The easiest workaround is to use `flush: post` for your watchers. It's been mentioned in other related issues but it's getting difficult to find now

One man’s “easiest” is another man’s “thousands of changes and infinite test surface”…

Might as well close this issue if there’s no intent to fix the discrepancy.
It has other implications to use `flush: post` because it changes the time when the watcher is called. I think it needs a fix. Calling a watcher of a component that is unmounted feels like a bug.
It's just a workaround 😉 . I'm adding it in case it helps some folks. Hopefully the PR can be merged for the next release

Just hit this issue, exact as described by OP. I was going crazy over what the cause was. but eventually tracked it down to the watcher and the only funny part of this story is that I had this issue before (but router-related) and had a comment pointing to this and other related threads 😅 

🤞 for the PR
